Alex — thanks for the note and great to hear the demo landed.

Quick answers up front: SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2026-12-31) attached; we also included a proposed audit/evidence cadence workbook and a starter set of MSA/order form redlines (OrderForm_BlueRiver_Redlines.docx).

High-level proposal (we can tweak per your security team's preferences):
- SOC 2: report attached (Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-Report-2026.pdf). We also provide an annual SOC attestation and keep an internal evidence library for common requests.
- Pen test / inspection: Redwood prefers staging-only or scoped production read-only evidence by default. If BlueRiver requires production access we ask for a 30-day notice + explicit scope (systems, IP ranges, accounts) and acceptance of ephemeral credentials + vendor-approved test window.
- Sampling vs full inspection: we support sampling for most audits. Typical approach: 1) weekly or bi-weekly snapshot exports for the first 8 weeks during go-live, then monthly snapshots thereafter; 2) ad-hoc requests escalated via an agreed SLA (72-hour turnaround for standard artifacts).

MSA redline notes included in the doc: limit "inspection rights" to systems in-scope for the contract, allow Redwood to redact secrets and third-party data, require mutual NDAs for on-site interviews, and a clause to limit vendor-provided access to read-only logs and artifacts unless otherwise negotiated.

Action items:
- Please review attachments and flag any must-have language for your legal/procurement.
- If you want a quick triage call, I can pull in Karthik (contracts) and Ben (security ops).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kim — copying a concise internal proposal to use as the basis for the MSA/order form redline. I attached a short summary doc (msa-redline-summary-20270520.docx) with suggested carve language. Key points we should propose to BlueRiver legal:

1) Notice & scope:
   - Replace unlimited "inspection rights" language with: "Customer may request an inspection of systems and records reasonably related to the Services, limited to systems identified in the Order Form and subject to 30 days' prior written notice and mutual scheduling."

2) Production access constraints:
   - Default to staging-only. If production access is required, require: (a) mutually agreed scope, (b) time-boxed window, (c) use of ephemeral accounts, (d) read-only access to logs and monitoring endpoints.

3) Sampling & evidence cadence:
   - Propose initial ramp: weekly snapshot exports for 8 weeks post-go-live (customer-provided list of tenant IDs), then monthly rolling snapshots.
   - SLA: Redwood will acknowledge evidence requests within 24 hours and target delivery within 72 hours for standard artifacts.

4) Redaction & third-party data:
   - Redwood may redact sensitive customer data and third-party PII prior to handing over artifacts; customer retains right to request additional context via secure channels.

5) Pen test coordination:
   - Vendor-led penetration tests permitted in staging without additional carveouts. For production tests, require 30 days' notice, written scope, and mutual approval of test plan.

Connor/Ben — anything to add on operational constraints or required teaching notes for the customer?

Karthik
Associate GC, Contracts
Redwood Inference
